issues.legal_issue: A suit by a licensor to recover possession from a gratuitous licensee is within the jurisdiction of the Small Causes Court when the property is within its territorial jurisdiction and no other applicable law excludes the suit.
material_facts: The occupants were permitted to use a bedroom without paying consideration and to share the hall and kitchen as common amenities.
After the permission was revoked, the occupants did not vacate, and the property owners sued to recover possession.
The suit concerned immovable property within the Small Causes Court’s territorial jurisdiction.
The Small Causes Court found the occupants to be gratuitous licensees and ordered eviction.
issues.conclusion: The term “licensee” in Section 41(1) of the PSCC Act includes a gratuitous licensee. The Small Causes Court may entertain and try a licensor’s suit for possession against such a licensee, subject to the exclusion in Section 41(2); the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 41(1) of the Presidency Small Causes Courts Act, 1882, as amended in 1976, gives the Small Causes Court jurisdiction over suits between licensors and licensees concerning recovery of possession of immovable property, irrespective of the subject matter’s value. Section 41(2) excludes matters to which specified or other applicable laws apply. The term “licensee” is not defined in the PSCC Act and is used in its wider, ordinary sense, consistent with the definition of licence in Section 52 of the Indian Easements Act, 1882, which does not require payment of consideration. It is not confined to the narrower, consideration-based meaning in Section 5(4A) of the Bombay Rent Act, 1947; suits governed by that Act fall within the Section 41(2) exclusion. In Mansukhlal Dhanraj Jain v. Eknath Vithal Ogale, the Court identified the relevant jurisdictional conditions as a suit between licensor and licensee (or landlord and tenant) relating to recovery of possession of property in Greater Bombay (or recovery of fees or rent). The Court also applied the ordinary-meaning approach to statutory interpretation and relied on State of Punjab v. Brig. Sukhjit Singh for the principle that payment of a licence fee is not essential to a licence.

rule.if: is_suit_by_property_grantor_against_permitted_occupant and suit_seeks_recovery_of_immovable_property_possession and property_within_small_causes_territory and occupant_is_gratuitous_licensee and not special_rent_regime_applies

predicates.is_suit_by_property_grantor_against_perm: A person who granted another permission to use property brings a suit against that occupant.
predicates.suit_seeks_recovery_of_immovable_propert: The suit seeks recovery of possession of immovable property.
predicates.property_within_small_causes_territory: The property is within the territorial jurisdiction of the Small Causes Court.
predicates.occupant_is_gratuitous_licensee: The occupant uses the property with the grantor’s permission and pays no consideration for that permission.
predicates.special_rent_regime_applies: The suit is governed by a special rent-control regime that displaces this court’s jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a property grantor sues a permitted occupant, the suit seeks possession of immovable property within the court’s territory, the occupant’s permission is gratuitous, and no special rent regime governs the suit, the Small Causes Court has jurisdiction.
